name: Deel
subcategory: HR, recruiting, payroll and workforce operations
tagline: Track contractor documents and approvals without employment, payroll, or payment services

pricing.notes: Official US Payroll monthly employee price; other products differ.

tiers.name: Find Talent
tiers.limits: $14 per worker/month for talent sourcing and hiring workflow

tiers.name: Contractor
tiers.limits: $49 per contractor/month for contracts, payments, compliance documents, and management

tiers.name: Contractor of Record
tiers.limits: Starts at $325 per contractor/month; Deel engages and manages the contractor

tiers.name: US PEO
tiers.limits: Starts at $125 per employee/month for US co-employment services

tiers.name: Employer of Record
tiers.limits: Starts at $599 per employee/month across 90+ countries

pricing.billingTerms: month-to-month public pricing; no public annual discount
pricing.hiddenCosts: Local severance, benefits, taxes, exchange rates, and payment methods can add cost. The current 3-month PEO platform-fee promotion requires a new order signed July 15–December 31, 2026 and a minimum 2-year term; the credit is applied at the end, and early termination requires repayment at list price.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Deel, track contractor documents and approvals without employment, payroll, or payment services. The hard boundary is global employment entities, contracts, payroll, compliance, payments, and immigration, plus compliance, payroll, and regulated integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Track contractor documents, maintain approvals and records, and export data without providing employment, payroll, or payment services or making employment decisions.
whatYouLose: global employment entities, contracts, payroll, compliance, payments, and immigration
identity checks and global employment infrastructure
ongoingBurden: sensitive data, access, retention, audit, payroll calculations, filings, benefits, employment law, incident response, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Deel because HR platforms survive because mistakes affect pay, benefits, immigration, and legal obligations, not because forms are difficult to render. The recurring cost buys sensitive data, access, retention, audit, payroll calculations, filings, benefits, employment law, incident response, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Frappe HR
priorArt.desc: Active open-source human-resources and payroll application built on Frappe.

alternatives.name: Connecteam Small Business Plan
alternatives.desc: Directory, documents, leave and onboarding for ten people; employee eleven is the business model.

facts.install: Hosted signup, then invite staff to the web and mobile apps
facts.dataFormat: Employee records, documents, schedules and time data in Connecteam's cloud; schedules and timesheets export to Excel, PDF, CSV or payroll-specific files
facts.gapVsPaid: It can hold records for ten people but provides none of Deel's country-specific contracts, compliance, payroll or contractor payments.

alternatives.name: OrangeHRM Starter
alternatives.desc: The old-school HR suite: records, leave, attendance and approvals, with a real server and no fashion budget.

facts.install: Use the free hosted Starter signup, or upload the release to an Apache/PHP/MySQL server and complete the web installer
facts.dataFormat: Hosted Starter keeps employee records in OrangeHRM's cloud; self-hosted Starter stores them in MySQL/MariaDB with uploaded files in application storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It tracks people and leave but does not replace Deel's legal entities, compliant contracts, payroll or international payments.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Apache, PHP and MySQL/MariaDB plus security and backups; the hosted path starts with a 30-day trial before conversion to lifetime-free Starter

alternatives.name: Horilla HR
alternatives.desc: Hire-to-leave HR in Docker; free forever means you own the updates and backups.

facts.install: Clone the stable 2.0 branch and run docker-compose up -d; a manual Django setup is also documented
facts.dataFormat: HR records in PostgreSQL by default, with uploaded media on server storage or optional Google Cloud Storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It has no employer-of-record, country compliance or money-movement service, and the HR server is yours to run.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker and production configuration: database credentials, secret key, allowed hosts, HTTPS, backups and mail remain the operator's job

alternatives.name: Frappe HR
alternatives.desc: A complete HR suite without the license bill; the server, backups and upgrades are now in your job description.

facts.install: Launch its Docker Compose stack, or install hrms and ERPNext into an existing Frappe Bench
facts.dataFormat: Each Frappe site has its own MariaDB database plus private/public files directories; backups are SQL dumps and file archives under the site
facts.gapVsPaid: It records HR data but cannot provide Deel's employer-of-record, localized contract, payroll and payment infrastructure.
facts.setupBlocker: The full Frappe/ERPNext stack brings Docker, MariaDB, Redis, proxy/TLS and version-compatible app upgrades

notes: Editorial comparison targets the US Payroll plan and a internal records tracker without payroll DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Deel in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: track contractor documents, maintain approvals and records, and export data without providing employment, payroll, or payment services or making employment decisions.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement employees, teams, roles, documents, leave requests, equipment, onboarding tasks, and acknowledgements.
Use least-privilege roles and log every read or change to sensitive records.
Add approval workflows, expiry reminders, export, retention, deletion holds, and encrypted backups.
Keep compensation fields optional and never calculate payroll, taxes, benefits, or statutory filings.
Provide a data dictionary and explain which fields should not be stored without legal review.
Ship Docker Compose, health checks, disaster recovery, and an emergency-access procedure.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out payroll calculation or money movement.
Deliberately leave out automated hiring decisions or applicant scoring.
Deliberately leave out tax, benefits, immigration, identity, and global-employment compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
